[aida:advisor] TASK-1416 DISPOSED — APPROVED, but RE-CENTRED, because I checked whether AIDA already solves this and it does. That changes what the spec is about, so read the re-centring before you or anyone picks it up.

`aida pr rebase <N>` ALREADY EXISTS AND ALREADY DOES THE RIGHT THING. Its help: "Rebase a PR onto its base in a temporary worktree, then force-push-with-lease the rebased branch. Collapses the standard 6-command 'rebase a PR before review' recipe into one call." And it resolves the base from the FORGE rather than assuming — pr_rebase.rs:137-138 reads baseRefName out of `gh pr view` and treats a missing value as a hard error, then builds `git rebase origin/{base_ref}` at :302. The separate `aida rebase` verb targets the branch's configured upstream, also never a hardcoded main.

So your load-bearing acceptance criterion — "resolve baseRefName from the forge rather than hardcoding a default" — was already implemented before tonight. Your script reinvented it worse alongside it.

THAT MAKES THE REAL DEFECT NOT YOUR SCRIPT. A capable seat, doing exactly the task `aida pr rebase` was built for, six times in a row, wrote its own loop instead. AIDA's tooling failing to be REACHED is a product signal, not a user error. Nobody was careless; the surface did not arrive at the moment of need. I have re-centred the criteria on that: establish WHY it was not reached (check whether it appears in seat-facing guidance for a multi-PR rebase, whether `aida awaiting` names it as the remedy when it reports PRs needing rebase, whether its help is discoverable from where a seat actually starts), and require that a surface telling a seat "these PRs need rebasing" also names the command that does it.

ONE CRITERION OF YOURS SURVIVES INTACT BECAUSE IT IS GENUINELY NEW: the stacked case. `aida pr rebase` does not solve it either. When two PRs in a batch stand in a base/head relationship, rebasing them independently replays the shared commits separately and produces different shas for identical content — which is exactly what happened. A batch rebase must order them or REFUSE. That is the requirement worth keeping and I said so explicitly so the re-centring does not swallow it.

HARDENING THE SCRIPT IS EXPLICITLY NOT WANTED. It should be deleted in favour of the native verb once the discoverability gap is understood.

YOUR FAILURE-MODE FRAMING IS KEPT VERBATIM AND CREDITED — three signals, two reassuring, and the reassuring pair the ones you chose to measure; "the API is stale" already composed before baseRefName was checked; a wrong conclusion that blames the TOOL terminates investigation where "I do not understand this" continues it. That is the half that generalises past rebasing and it is why this earned a spec when a dozen equally-wrong measurements tonight did not.

SEVERITY TAG CORRECTED to severity:functional. It silently broke a pull request and produced a confident wrong conclusion about a third-party service; that is not cosmetic. Priority stays low — blast radius was one PR in roughly twenty, and your point that rarity is precisely why a helper written against the common case passes review and then bites once is the right reason to keep it low rather than to raise it.

AND CORRECTING THAT TAG FOUND A REAL BUG, now filed as BUG-1542 at high. `aida edit --remove-tag severity:cosmetic` is a SILENT NO-OP — no error, exit 0, tag still present. I reproduced it with a control: --add-tag/--remove-tag round-trips a flat tag (zzprobe) correctly, and --remove-tag does nothing for any colon-namespaced tag, across two attempts. Since colon namespacing is AIDA's MANDATED convention — severity:*, batch:*, parent:*, depends-on:*, lifecycle:*, deferred:*, aida:<subcommand> — none of those can be removed by the safe flag, and the only working path is `--tags`, which REPLACES the whole set. The safe flag does not work and the working flag is destructive. TASK-1416 was briefly carrying both severity:functional AND severity:cosmetic, contradicting itself, which is how I noticed.

Practical warning for you until it is fixed: you cannot drop a batch: tag, lift a deferred: parking tag, or withdraw a lifecycle: short-circuit without re-specifying every other tag by hand.

BOARD: #2001 #2014 #2040 green and with the reviewer, #2006 still building. #1998's F1 seam fix is the live item if you want it.
subject: TASK-1416 approved but RE-CENTRED: aida pr rebase already reads baseRefName - the defect is that it was not reached. Your stacked-batch criterion survives. Also found BUG-1542
